question: What is the most important approach for a nurse caring for a patient who has undergone FGM?

options.A: Express immediate shock and pity for the patient's condition
options.B: Question the patient aggressively about who performed the act
options.C: Use a trauma-informed, non-judgmental approach to build trust
options.D: Avoid performing any physical examinations to prevent awkwardness

explanation: Wonderful! Creating a safe, empathetic environment lets the patient open up about their health without feeling judged or ashamed.

question: What term describes the official power attached to a management role that lets you give orders and make decisions?

options.A: Accountability
options.B: Authority
options.C: Specialisation
options.D: Responsibility

explanation: Authority is that official backing of your position that says, 'Yes, you have the green light to direct this process and make the call.'

question: Which healthcare professional helps a patient with severe swallowing difficulties eat safely?

options.A: Speech pathologist
options.B: Biomedical engineer
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Radiologic technologist

explanation: Don't let the title fool you—speech therapists are experts in mouth muscles, chewing, and safe swallowing (dysphagia) too!

question: How can an unusually long fallopian tube affect the movement of an egg?

options.A: It slows down movement and can trap the egg inside
options.B: It stops the uterus from making female hormones
options.C: It completely stops the ovary from releasing eggs
options.D: It speeds up movement so much that the egg is destroyed

explanation: When a tube is extra long or twisted, the muscle movements are less efficient, making it easy for the slow-moving egg to get stuck. You've got this!

question: Why is a blame-free reporting culture so helpful for improving safety on hospital wards?

options.A: It speeds up the process of investigating patient complaints about pain
options.B: It allows the hospital to avoid paying for expensive safety-engineered needles
options.C: It encourages staff to report near-misses and hazards so systemic fixes can be made
options.D: It ensures that nurses never face disciplinary action for deliberate negligence

explanation: When staff feel safe speaking up without fear of being shouted at or punished, everyone can work together to fix dangerous workplace problems.

question: Why do doctors most commonly perform a colostomy?

options.A: To permanently cure long-term constipation without changing diet
options.B: To bypass or remove a diseased or damaged part of the bowel
options.C: To allow direct medicine administration into the bloodstream
options.D: To increase the length of the small intestine for better food absorption

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like severe infection, injury, or cancer mean we need to safely divert waste away from a sick section of the large intestine.

question: Which gland releases cortisol when signaled by the pituitary gland during stress?

options.A: Adrenal cortex
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Pineal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The outer layer of your adrenal glands (right above your kidneys) is called the adrenal cortex, and it pumps out cortisol to help you handle stress.

question: What is the primary goal of performing last offices?

options.A: To treat the body with dignity and respect
options.B: To sanitize the hospital ward completely
options.C: To train junior student nurses on anatomy
options.D: To prepare the body immediately for autopsy

explanation: Last offices are carried out primarily to ensure the deceased person is handled with respect, care, and dignity. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic drug monitoring?

options.A: To confirm that the medication is producing the desired clinical effect
options.B: To test if the patient is secretly selling their prescription
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department bills the patient correctly
options.D: To prove that the physician chose the cheapest available brand

explanation: We monitor to make sure the drug is actually helping the patient heal and not causing trouble. Spot on!

question: What is the main goal of musculoskeletal rehabilitation?

options.A: To accelerate the natural clotting of fractured bones
options.B: To completely eliminate all chronic joint inflammation
options.C: To restore functional capacity and independence
options.D: To replace lost surgical muscle mass with scar tissue

explanation: Great job! Rehab is all about helping patients get back on their feet so they can do their daily activities and live independently.

question: Which test gives the final confirmation that a patient has active lung TB?

options.A: Physical auscultation of bilateral lung sounds
options.B: Routine complete blood count and electrolyte panel
options.C: Measurement of resting blood pressure and pulse rate
options.D: Sputum culture and acid-fast bacilli smear testing

explanation: Checking the patient's sputum for acid-fast bacilli or growing the germs in a lab gives the definitive proof needed to confirm active TB.

question: A nurse wants to check old hospital files of patients who took a specific blood pressure drug five years ago to see who developed kidney issues. What kind of study is this?

options.A: Experimental trial
options.B: Retrospective cohort study
options.C: Cross-sectional survey
options.D: Case-control study

explanation: Well done! This design starts with a past exposure (the drug taken years ago) and tracks forward through old records to see what health outcomes happened.

question: What is the best way to help an awake, intubated patient communicate with you?

options.A: Using communication boards or writing tablets
options.B: Asking the patient to whisper loudly around the tube
options.C: Relying entirely on family members to translate lip movements
options.D: Temporarily deflating the cuff on the tube so they can talk

explanation: Because the breathing tube sits right through the vocal cords, speaking is impossible. Simple writing pads or picture boards are a nurse's best friend here!

question: What spare equipment must always stay right at the bedside for a patient with a tracheostomy?

options.A: A set of surgical scalpels and sutures
options.B: A backup mechanical ventilator machine
options.C: A spare tracheostomy tube and obturator
options.D: An extra oxygen tank and nasal cannula

explanation: Safety first! A matching spare tube and obturator must always be ready at the bedside in case of an emergency replacement.

question: Why do we grab a cold pack immediately after someone suffers a fresh joint sprain?

options.A: To heat up the deep tissue and relax tight tendons
options.B: To stimulate rapid cell division in the bone
options.C: To dilate vessels and increase local bleeding
options.D: To constrict blood vessels and reduce swelling

explanation: Spot on! Cold causes vasoconstriction (narrowing the vessels), which slows down blood flow to the fresh injury so it doesn't blow up into a huge swelling.

question: What is a major risk for patients taking immune checkpoint inhibitors (immunotherapy)?

options.A: The medication causes immediate permanent sterility in both male and female patients.
options.B: The boosted immune system may attack normal, healthy organs, causing widespread inflammation.
options.C: The drug destroys bone marrow production completely, requiring lifelong platelet transfusions.
options.D: The patient will instantly lose all hair follicles within forty-eight hours of the first dose.

explanation: You got it! Reviving the immune system is great for fighting cancer, but sometimes the revved-up immune cells accidentally attack healthy organs like the lungs or gut.

question: Which type of vitamin can easily build up to toxic levels if taken in excess over time?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.C: Amino acid supplements
options.D: Plant-based minerals

explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in body fat instead of being peed out quickly, taking too many of them over time can lead to a harmful buildup.

question: A patient with severe fatigue insists on cleaning their whole house in one go, leaving them bedridden for days afterward. What nursing advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid all movement for the next month to let muscles heal.
options.B: Break chores into small parts and rest between each task.
options.C: Increase caffeine intake to maintain speed through the cleaning.
options.D: Perform all cleaning tasks immediately after waking up.

explanation: You're learning great clinical judgment! Splitting big tasks into smaller chunks and resting in between helps patients break the exhausting 'boom-and-bust' cycle.

question: How do State Health Insurance Agencies usually differ from the federal NHIA initiative?

options.A: They only provide care for surgical emergencies in private clinics
options.B: They prohibit civil servants from accessing any form of medical care
options.C: They focus heavily on covering informal sector workers and rural dwellers in their states
options.D: They are funded exclusively by grants from foreign international banks

explanation: You're getting it! While federal schemes started with government workers, state agencies make special efforts to reach traders, artisans, and rural villagers.

question: What type of medication is commonly given to help patients get rid of extra fluid?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Diuretics
options.C: Analgesics
options.D: Anticoagulants

explanation: You nailed it! Diuretics (often called 'water pills') prompt the kidneys to flush out extra salt and water.

question: Why can a strong family preference for male children negatively impact a mother's health?

options.A: It forces women into continuous pregnancies until a son is born, straining their bodies
options.B: It reduces the financial income of the father drastically
options.C: It causes hospitals to refuse treatment to female newborns
options.D: It encourages the use of modern contraceptives

explanation: Constant, closely spaced pregnancies driven by the pressure to have a son really wear down a mother's body and deplete her nutrients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is a classic sign of cervical irritation that often shows up after sexual intercourse?

options.A: Severe lower back stiffness
options.B: Post-coital bleeding
options.C: Intermittent abdominal swelling
options.D: Sudden loss of bladder control

explanation: Spot on! When the cervix is inflamed and fragile, any physical touch or rubbing during sex can easily trigger light bleeding.

question: What is a common social penalty for a woman spotted visiting a family planning clinic in a stigmatized community?

options.A: Being labeled as promiscuous by neighbors
options.B: Receiving a free scholarship for her children
options.C: Being appointed as the village head
options.D: Winning a local agricultural prize

explanation: Correct! Community stigma unfortunately leads people to make false assumptions about the moral character of women seeking birth control.

question: A patient is feeling very carsick on a bus ride. Which receptors should an effective anti-nausea drug target?

options.A: Opioid and cannabinoid
options.B: Substance P and neurokinin
options.C: Serotonin and dopamine
options.D: Histamine and acetylcholine

explanation: Well done! Motion sickness starts in the inner ear's balance center, which heavily relies on histamine and acetylcholine pathways. Blocking these stops the dizziness and nausea!

question: What is the golden rule for feeding an infant during their first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding with no other foods or liquids
options.B: Cow milk combined with fresh fruit juices
options.C: Formula milk mixed with clean local spring water
options.D: Breastmilk supplemented with thin cereal porridges

explanation: You got it! Breastmilk alone for the first six months provides all the nutrients and infection-fighting protection a baby needs.

question: Why are old writings from figures like Hippocrates and Pliny so important to occupational health?

options.A: They established the first formal nursing schools in Europe
options.B: They proved that workplace injuries were caused by poor hygiene
options.C: They forced emperors to pass the first fair labor acts
options.D: They linked specific jobs directly to certain physical illnesses

explanation: These early scholars were the first to notice how certain jobs—like working with lead or sulfur—made workers sick. It laid the foundation for modern occupational health!

question: What should you as a nurse do right away if a drug order written in the patient's chart is unclear?

options.A: Consult the patient to see what medication they usually prefer taking
options.B: Withhold the drug and contact the prescriber to clarify the order
options.C: Ask a senior student nurse to guess the correct intended dose
options.D: Administer the standard adult dose to avoid missing the time schedule

explanation: You are legally responsible for the medications you give. Never guess or act on an unclear prescription—always pause, hold the drug, and call the doctor to clarify.

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what pushes someone to finally adopt a new health habit?

options.A: Being forced by local law enforcement officers to visit the clinic
options.B: Forgetting that diseases exist in their local environment
options.C: Receiving financial payment for every health clinic visit
options.D: Believing the health threat is serious and the benefits outweigh the barriers

explanation: Exactly! People are ready to make a change when they see a real personal risk and feel that the solution is easy enough to do.

question: What makes the theatre (operating suite) feel a lot more intense and risky than a regular medical-surgical ward?

options.A: It completely lacks water and basic soap for handwashing
options.B: Every single patient has a severe infectious disease
options.C: Nurses never get to sit down or take tea breaks
options.D: It brings together fast emergencies, heavy equipment, and tight spaces

explanation: The theatre is a unique environment! Mixing advanced gadgets, high-pressure moments, and a confined space naturally creates extra physical and mental challenges.

question: What type of cartilage connects the bones in a symphysis joint, like the pubic symphysis?

options.A: Elastic cartilage
options.B: Calcified bone matrix
options.C: Fibrocartilage
options.D: Dense fibrous connective tissue

explanation: Spot on! Symphysis joints use tough pads of fibrocartilage to absorb shocks while giving just a tiny bit of flexibility.

question: Which of these traditional food practices actually goes hand-in-hand with modern science?

options.A: Combining grains and legumes for complete protein
options.B: Avoiding all liquids during a bout of severe diarrhea
options.C: Giving only sugary water to a newborn infant
options.D: Starving a patient completely to cure a high fever

explanation: Mixing grains and legumes (like rice and beans) is a brilliant traditional practice that supplies all essential amino acids our bodies need!

question: How is true sputum different from ordinary saliva?

options.A: Saliva is thick and colored green or yellow due to infection
options.B: Sputum is produced entirely by glands inside the oral cavity
options.C: Saliva contains high amounts of blood and cellular debris
options.D: Sputum comes from deep in the lungs and lower respiratory tract

explanation: Saliva is just mouth fluid, but sputum comes coughing up from the lungs and bronchial tubes, which is what the lab needs to see.

question: Why does community health nursing go beyond just giving care at the bedside?

options.A: To reduce the number of trained doctors needed in clinics
options.B: To replace traditional hospital treatments entirely
options.C: To address environmental and social factors affecting health
options.D: To focus exclusively on rare surgical complications

explanation: Spot on! Things like housing, clean water, and daily living conditions shape a population's health just as much as medicine does.

question: What does angiotensin II normally do to your blood vessels?

options.A: Widens the blood vessels
options.B: Destroys blood platelets
options.C: Relaxes the vessel walls
options.D: Narrows the blood vessels

explanation: Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor—it squeezes your blood vessels tight to quickly push your blood pressure back up.

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital!

question: How does breastfeeding prevent pregnancy during the early postpartum period?

options.A: Feeding creates a physical barrier in the uterus
options.B: Prolactin directly destroys mature sperm cells
options.C: Suckling stimulates hormones that suppress ovulation
options.D: Breast milk changes the pH of the vaginal canal

explanation: Frequent infant suckling keeps prolactin levels high, which naturally inhibits the release of hormones needed for ovulation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing reproductive health programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of surplus modern hospitals in every village
options.B: Shortages of trained healthcare staff in rural community clinics
options.C: Cultural or religious resistance to certain family planning methods
options.D: Financial barriers caused by out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: Spot on! Rural areas actually struggle with a lack of enough hospitals and clinics, making the idea of 'surplus hospitals in every village' completely false.

question: How do barrier contraceptives help protect against cervical irritation?

options.A: They physically block infectious microorganisms from reaching the cervical mucosa.
options.B: They permanently seal the transformation zone to stop cellular changes.
options.C: They eliminate all normal bacteria living inside the reproductive tract.
options.D: They automatically increase natural estrogen levels in the vaginal canal.

explanation: Well done! Barrier methods like condoms act like a shield, stopping germs from making direct contact with the cervix.

question: What is the best way for a community health nurse to handle local rumors about vaccine safety?

options.A: Engage community leaders in open dialogue and health education
options.B: Ignore the community complaints and focus only on paperwork
options.C: Scold parents who ask questions about vaccine ingredients
options.D: Close down the immunization clinic until rumors stop spreading

explanation: Teaming up with trusted community leaders and providing respectful, clear health talks is the best way to clear up fears and build trust.

question: Which nutrients are especially vital for a patient healing from a broken bone?

options.A: Calcium, vitamin D, and protein
options.B: Vitamin C and simple sugars
options.C: Sodium and complex starches
options.D: Iron and fluid electrolytes

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D make the bone hard and strong again, while protein builds the framework for the new tissue. Diet plays a huge role in recovery!

question: What is the main goal of teaching Kegel exercises to someone with urinary incontinence?

options.A: To strengthen the pelvic floor muscles supporting the bladder
options.B: To relax the abdominal wall during a physical exam
options.C: To stretch the ureters and widen the urinary tract
options.D: To increase total daily urine production in the kidneys

explanation: Kegels tone up those pelvic floor muscles, giving the patient much better control over when they go.

question: Which of the following describes Type I FGM?

options.A: Cutting away both the clitoris and labia majora
options.B: Partial or total removal of the clitoris
options.C: Creating a seal over the vaginal opening
options.D: Piercing or scraping the labia majora

explanation: Type I focuses on removing part or all of the clitoris. You'll see this classification often in community health nursing!

question: A patient with diabetes has a fasting blood sugar of 55 mg/dL and is shaky and confused. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?

options.A: Kidney failure causing a backup of metabolic waste
options.B: A normal reaction to an overnight fasting period
options.C: Dehydration from drinking too much plain water
options.D: Brain glucose deprivation from low blood sugar

explanation: When blood sugar drops too low, the brain lacks energy, causing neurological symptoms like confusion and shaking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the main goal of taking a nutritional supplement?

options.A: To add extra dietary ingredients to a person's daily intake
options.B: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.C: To completely replace the need for eating solid foods
options.D: To act as a prescribed pharmaceutical medication

explanation: Supplements are meant to add to your normal meals, not replace them! They give your body a little extra boost of vitamins or minerals when needed.

question: Which nurse behavior is most likely to drive a teenager away from a health clinic permanently?

options.A: Empathetic counseling
options.B: Moralizing and scolding
options.C: Active listening
options.D: Warm greeting

explanation: Teens are super sensitive to criticism. If they expect to be judged or lectured, they'll avoid getting the care they need.

question: A client with severe hypertension comes to your primary health post asking for combined oral contraceptive pills. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the client to a facility that offers safe, non-hormonal or progestin-only alternatives
options.B: Dispense the pills with instructions to monitor blood pressure at home
options.C: Perform a surgical tubal ligation immediately at the primary health post
options.D: Refuse service entirely and tell the client to use no protection

explanation: Combined pills contain estrogen, which isn't safe for high blood pressure. Getting her to a higher facility helps her find a safer method!

question: Which part of the brain acts as our master biological clock?

options.A: The suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.B: The pituitary gland
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: Think of the suprachiasmatic nucleus as your body's personal timekeeper! Located in the hypothalamus, it takes in light signals from your eyes to keep your daily body rhythms on track.

question: Why is patient teaching so important when managing chronic open-angle glaucoma?

options.A: Patients have to perform mini-surgeries at home
options.B: Eye drops must be mixed with clean water before every use
options.C: The disease is usually painless, so patients might skip lifelong treatment
options.D: The medications cure the underlying nerve damage quickly

explanation: Because chronic glaucoma doesn't hurt, patients often feel totally fine and forget to take their daily drops. Good teaching helps them see why consistency is life-saving for their vision.

question: What type of food should make up the biggest part of an adolescent girl's daily energy intake?

options.A: Refined table sugars
options.B: Pure protein powders
options.C: Saturated animal fats
options.D: Complex carbohydrates

explanation: Wonderful! Complex carbs (like yam, brown rice, and beans) give growing teens steady, lasting energy and healthy fiber.

question: What is a major money-related barrier that often stops women from accessing healthcare?

options.A: Financial dependence due to lack of property and inheritance rights
options.B: Universal health insurance plans that exclude female patients
options.C: Mandatory employment taxes collected only from female workers
options.D: Higher hospital admission fees charged specifically for women

explanation: When cultural or legal rules prevent women from owning land or earning their own money, they have to rely completely on others, making medical bills nearly impossible to pay.

question: What is an important safety tip for any patient taking a medication that causes drowsiness?

options.A: Exercise vigorously right after each dose.
options.B: Take the medication only on an empty stomach.
options.C: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery.
options.D: Stop drinking all fluids during the daytime.

explanation: Drowsy meds slow down reflexes. Always remind patients to avoid driving or working with heavy machines until they know how the drug affects them.

question: You need to give a routine vaccine to a healthy 12-month-old baby. Which injection site is best?

options.A: Dorsogluteal
options.B: Ventrogluteal
options.C: Vastus lateralis
options.D: Deltoid

explanation: Spot on! The vastus lateralis (thigh muscle) is nice and plump in little infants, making it the go-to, safe spot for routine baby immunizations.

question: How does dopamine affect the indirect pathway to help us move?

options.A: It activates the indirect pathway to freeze all motor actions
options.B: It suppresses the indirect pathway to reduce braking on movement
options.C: It turns dopamine into acetylcholine
options.D: It destroys the subthalamic nucleus immediately

explanation: Think of the indirect pathway as a brake on your movements. Dopamine steps on the gas (direct pathway) and eases off the brakes (indirect pathway), making it smooth and easy for you to move!

question: For about how long can an unfertilized egg survive after being released during ovulation?

options.A: 12 to 24 hours
options.B: 5 to 7 days
options.C: 48 to 72 hours
options.D: 1 month

explanation: An egg has a very short shelf life—just 12 to 24 hours after ovulation—which is why timing is everything for fertilization!

question: Which special cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: Parietal cells
options.C: Goblet cells
options.D: Mucus neck cells

explanation: Parietal cells are the acid-makers of the stomach, and they also produce intrinsic factor which helps your body absorb vitamin B12.

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the digestive tract?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach, while peristalsis happens in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation relies on skeletal muscle, while peristalsis uses smooth muscle.
options.C: Segmentation stops digestion, while peristalsis speeds up absorption.
options.D: Segmentation mixes food back and forth, while peristalsis pushes food forward.

explanation: Think of peristalsis as a wave pushing food down a slide, while segmentation is more like stirring soup back and forth to mix it thoroughly with digestive juices!

question: What is the best way to start talking to a patient who has a hearing impairment?

options.A: Stand behind the patient and speak loudly to surprise them into listening
options.B: Turn on the television to provide background noise for a normal atmosphere
options.C: Get the patient's attention visually and face them directly before speaking
options.D: Keep the room dark so the patient can concentrate entirely on sound

explanation: You're a natural! Facing them and getting their attention first lets them use your facial expressions and lip movements to understand you better.

question: Which of these common infections is caused by a bacterium?

options.A: Human Papillomavirus
options.B: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.C: Herpes Simplex Virus
options.D: Trichomonas vaginalis

explanation: Chlamydia is a bacterial infection. Remember: bacterial bugs can be knocked out with the right antibiotics!

question: A patient is admitted to the emergency room with extreme restlessness, high blood pressure, and dilated pupils after taking a street drug. Which substance class is most likely involved?

options.A: Opioids
options.B: Depressants
options.C: Stimulants
options.D: Sedatives

explanation: Stimulants speed up the central nervous system, causing signs like high blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and dilated pupils. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h3)

question: Where are the developing egg follicles primarily housed within the ovary?

options.A: The outer cortex
options.B: The fallopian infundibulum
options.C: The broad ligament
options.D: The inner medulla

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains the ovarian follicles in various stages of development. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is another common name for Type III FGM?

options.A: Excision
options.B: Defibulation
options.C: Clitoridectomy
options.D: Infibulation

explanation: Type III is widely called infibulation because the procedure creates a sealed covering over the vaginal opening.

question: As the baby's head extends to be born, which bone acts as the pivot point?

options.A: The pubic symphysis
options.B: The coccyx bone
options.C: The ischial spine
options.D: The maternal sacrum

explanation: Correct! The baby's head pivots right under the mother's pubic bone, allowing it to lift upward and out into the world.

question: What is the golden rule for traction weights on a patient's bed?

options.A: Allow the weights to hang freely without touching the floor
options.B: Rest the weights on the bed frame to give the patient a break
options.C: Lift the weights manually during every nursing shift change
options.D: Disconnect the weights whenever the patient wants to turn

explanation: Weights must always hang freely in the air. If they touch the bed or floor, the pulling force stops working on the bone!

question: Which of the following actions represents a breach of nursing ethics in reproductive health?

options.A: Discussing a patient's private HIV test result with coworkers in the cafeteria
options.B: Providing confidential contraceptive counseling to an unmarried adult woman
options.C: Reporting a case of child abuse to the appropriate hospital social worker
options.D: Refusing to perform female genital mutilation because it is harmful

explanation: Sharing private patient information outside the direct care team violates confidentiality and patient rights. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: A woman who has given birth many times is at 32 weeks pregnant and reports painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Uterine rupture
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Incompetent cervix
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Painless bleeding in the third trimester is a classic sign of placenta previa, which is more common when past births have caused changes or scarring in the womb.

question: What measuring device should nurses recommend for giving liquid medicines safely to children?

options.A: A plastic coffee stirrer
options.B: An oral dosing syringe
options.C: A large soup ladle
options.D: A standard kitchen teaspoon

explanation: Oral syringes give precise dosing accuracy, whereas regular kitchen spoons vary wildly in size and liquid capacity.

question: Why do patients with severe fluid overload often develop crackling sounds in their lungs?

options.A: Dehydration causes the bronchial tubes to narrow and whistle
options.B: Fluid backs up into the pulmonary air sacs and airways
options.C: The chest muscles weaken from holding extra body weight
options.D: The patient develops a secondary bacterial pneumonia infection

explanation: Spot on! When the plumbing system is overloaded, fluid backs up into the tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs, making a crackling sound when they breathe.

question: What does the term 'hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy' mean?

options.A: Sudden inflammation of the peripheral nerve endings
options.B: An infection of the lining surrounding the spinal cord
options.C: Brain injury caused by oxygen and blood deprivation
options.D: A chronic degenerative disease of the liver tissue

explanation: Let's break down the big words: 'hypoxic' (low oxygen), 'ischemic' (low blood flow), and 'encephalopathy' (brain trouble). Put it together, and it's brain injury from lack of oxygen and blood!

question: Why must metformin be withheld from patients receiving an iodine contrast agent?

options.A: To stop the contrast dye from crystallizing inside the stomach lining
options.B: To keep the patient's blood pressure from dropping too low during the test
options.C: To prevent the dangerous buildup of lactic acidosis if kidneys struggle
options.D: To ensure the x-ray machine captures a clear picture of the pancreas

explanation: If the contrast temporarily impairs kidney function, metformin can accumulate and trigger a severe metabolic complication called lactic acidosis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why do middlemen often add to the final retail cost of food items?

options.A: The government requires a special tax for every person who touches food
options.B: Farmers pay brokers a fine for picking crops too early
options.C: Each handler adds a markup to cover their services and risks
options.D: Middlemen store food in expensive international warehouses

explanation: Every intermediary along the chain charges for their labor, transport, and potential losses, raising the cumulative price. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h5)

question: What do we call the emotional tiredness and burnout nurses feel from caring for suffering patients day after day?

options.A: Perceived loss
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Complex mourning
options.D: Compassion fatigue

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when we absorb so much patient trauma and stress without taking time to recharge ourselves.

question: A new mother at a health post starts bleeding heavily and looks dizzy and pale. What are your first nursing steps?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stand up and walk around to stimulate circulation
options.B: Apply a warm compress to the patient's forehead and offer oral fluids
options.C: Wait quietly for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.D: Perform uterine massage, give oxytocin, and prepare for emergency referral

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is an emergency. Massaging the uterus and giving oxytocin helps it contract while you arrange urgent transfer.

question: What is a key characteristic of direct ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: It produces an inverted image that must be flipped mentally
options.B: It requires a heavy head-mounted light source worn by the examiner
options.C: It provides an upright, magnified view of a small retinal area
options.D: It gives a complete wide-angle view of the entire peripheral retina

explanation: Direct ophthalmoscopy uses a handy device to give an upright image magnified roughly 15 times, though it covers a narrower field than indirect methods. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h3)

question: How do nurses primarily bridge the gap between public health policy and the local community?

options.A: By manufacturing pharmaceuticals in industrial laboratory settings
options.B: By working directly with individuals and families as educators and care providers
options.C: By writing national healthcare laws and passing public health budgets
options.D: By managing international trade agreements for medical supplies

explanation: Spot on! Nurses interact face-to-face with community members every day, making them the best messengers for public health guidelines.

question: You see an infected villager walking toward the local drinking pond to soothe a burning leg blister. What should you do first?

options.A: Stop the person from entering the water and provide safe filtered water
options.B: Advise the villager to wash the wound thoroughly inside the well
options.C: Pull the entire Guinea worm out rapidly with surgical forceps
options.D: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics to kill the worm

explanation: Fantastic nursing judgment! Keeping infected limbs out of community water sources stops the transmission cycle right in its tracks. You're going to make an amazing nurse!

question: Where does primary-level rehabilitation usually happen?

options.A: In high-tech national trauma centers
options.B: At large university teaching hospitals only
options.C: At local health posts and primary health centers
options.D: Inside specialized tertiary surgical wards

explanation: That's right! Primary-level care is the closest healthcare point to the community, handling basic checks and early support right where people live.

question: Why must nurse managers actively supervise instead of just writing policies on paper?

options.A: Written policies alone cannot guarantee staff will follow them safely
options.B: Nurse managers have no other administrative duties assigned to them
options.C: Staff nurses prefer having constant supervision during every shift
options.D: Hospital accreditation bodies legally require daily verbal check-ins

explanation: Having a policy on paper is a good start, but checking actual practice ensures everyone is safe and rules are followed in real clinical situations.

question: A nurse is feeling burnt out after seeing multiple emergency cases. Which type of support is best?

options.A: Formative supervision
options.B: Restorative supervision
options.C: Administrative supervision
options.D: Normative supervision

explanation: When clinical work drains you emotionally, restorative supervision steps in to restore your peace of mind and help you cope with stress.

question: How can health facilities best fix the problem of staff underreporting due to a fear of blame?

options.A: By firing every nurse who makes a minor documentation error
options.B: By hiding all disease statistics from the government ministry
options.C: By stopping all surveillance activities during busy seasons
options.D: By fostering a supportive, blame-free work culture that values data

explanation: When staff know they won't be unfairly punished for honest mistakes, they are much more open and accurate with their reporting. Spot on!

question: Why do doctors check for other issues like thyroid problems when evaluating someone for andropause?

options.A: Thyroid hormones directly destroy circulating testosterone
options.B: Thyroid problems can cause symptoms that mimic testosterone deficiency
options.C: Hypothyroidism stops the testicles from producing sperm
options.D: Thyroid disease prevents sex hormone-binding globulin from working

explanation: Many conditions like thyroid issues cause the same tiredness and mood changes, so ruling them out helps us make sure it's really andropause.

question: When old skin flakes off after a minor scrape heals, which layer is mostly shedding?

options.A: Stratum corneum
options.B: Stratum basale
options.C: Stratum granulosum
options.D: Stratum spinosum

explanation: Spot on! The stratum corneum is our outermost layer made of tough, dead cells that naturally flake off over time. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main focus of the 'Study' phase?

options.A: Buying new computers for the nursing station
options.B: Firing staff members whose tests did not show improvement
options.C: Analyzing data and comparing results to initial predictions
options.D: Starting a brand new project without checking the old one

explanation: Fantastic! In the Study phase, we look at our notes to see if our new idea actually matched what we hoped would happen.

question: Testicular cancer is most commonly diagnosed in which age group?

options.A: Young men aged 15 to 35
options.B: Middle-aged men aged 50 to 65
options.C: Pre-pubertal boys under 10
options.D: Elderly men over 75 years

explanation: Good to know! Unlike many other cancers, testicular cancer hits younger guys, which is why teaching self-exams to this group is so vital.

question: You notice clear fluid draining from the nose of a patient who just had pituitary surgery. What is a quick bedside test to see if it is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: Smell the fluid to check for a sharp ammonia or vinegar odor.
options.B: Check the exact temperature of the fluid with a digital probe.
options.C: Shine an ultraviolet light directly onto the wet dressing.
options.D: Test the fluid for glucose using a standard urine dipstick.

explanation: CSF is rich in glucose, whereas normal nasal mucus is not! Touching a glucose test strip to the drainage is a fast, clever way at the bedside to check for a CSF leak.

question: What is the primary goal in the medical management of acute gastroenteritis?

options.A: Replacing lost fluids and electrolytes
options.B: Stopping the bowel movements immediately
options.C: Placing the patient on a strict zero-food diet
options.D: Giving strong antibiotics to kill all viruses

explanation: Preventing or correcting dehydration is the single most important intervention to save lives in gastroenteritis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: A male patient looks very distressed, but insists nothing is wrong because 'men do not complain.' What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Refuse to treat him until he admits he is feeling emotionally weak
options.B: Ignore his emotional state and focus only on his physical blood pressure
options.C: Acknowledge his distress gently and validate that seeking help is a strength
options.D: Tell him he is acting too sensitive and should behave like a strong man

explanation: Wonderful! Validating our male patients helps break down harmful ideas that stopping to care for mental health makes them weak.

question: In what way can a healthy disagreement actually help a nursing unit?

options.A: By completely eliminating the need for multidisciplinary meetings
options.B: By ensuring all nurses agree on every clinical decision
options.C: By reducing the total number of daily patient admissions
options.D: By encouraging creative problem-solving and exposing workflow flaws

explanation: Not all conflict is bad! Healthy debates let team members point out broken workflows and find smarter, safer ways to care for patients.

question: What happens to a joint capsule when severe inflammation occurs?

options.A: It completely dries up and fuses the bones together
options.B: It stops producing all blood supply to the limb
options.C: It produces excess fluid, creating a joint effusion
options.D: It turns into hard bone tissue overnight

explanation: Inflammation inside the joint lining triggers swelling and fluid buildup, which is called an effusion. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why do pharmaceutical companies often need special incentives to develop orphan drugs?

options.A: Rare disease medications are made only from plant roots
options.B: Doctors refuse to prescribe drugs that treat uncommon illnesses
options.C: Government laws forbid selling rare disease drugs for money
options.D: The small number of patients makes traditional profit difficult

explanation: Developing a drug costs millions, but with very few patients to buy it, companies need incentives to offset research costs. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h7)

question: How does an untreated lower genital infection turn into Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Fungi colonize the bladder wall and obstruct the normal flow of urine
options.B: Bacteria enter the systemic circulation and settle permanently in the heart valves
options.C: Pathogens ascend from the cervix through the uterus into the fallopian tubes and pelvic cavity
options.D: Viruses alter bone marrow production, leading to severe immunological suppression

explanation: PID happens when bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix, causing widespread inflammation in the upper reproductive organs.

question: On a standard WHO growth chart, what does the bottom (horizontal) line represent?

options.A: The weight of the child
options.B: The age of the child
options.C: The mid-upper arm circumference
options.D: The height of the child

explanation: Think of the horizontal axis as time passing (age), while the vertical axis shows the measurement like weight or height.

question: What do social systems like schools and local clinics do for a community?

options.A: They prevent all members from ever experiencing chronic illnesses
options.B: They replace the need for individual family support structures
options.C: They dictate the exact weather patterns and agricultural seasons
options.D: They provide the organized institutions needed to meet basic human needs

explanation: Exactly! Social systems are like the pillars of a society—hospitals, schools, and markets work together to keep everyday life running smoothly.

question: What is your main job as a clinic nurse when it comes to family planning reporting?

options.A: Purchasing international medical supplies directly
options.B: Manufacturing contraceptive commodities for the district
options.C: Auditing national health ministry budgets annually
options.D: Gathering and recording service data at the clinic level

explanation: You've got this! Nurses right there at the clinic are the vital first link in capturing client visits and service data accurately.

question: Which of these is a chemical barrier part of our innate defense?

options.A: Cytotoxic T-cell activation
options.B: Keratin in the outer skin layer
options.C: Lysozyme in tears and saliva
options.D: Antibodies produced by plasma cells

explanation: You're right! Lysozyme is a natural germ-killer found in our tears and saliva that breaks open bacterial walls.

question: A new mother complains of a severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain 3 days after birth. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Discharge her home to rest
options.B: Report these signs immediately as possible postpartum pre-eclampsia
options.C: Tell her to stop breastfeeding until the headache clears
options.D: Reassure her that it is just normal tiredness

explanation: Excellent catch! Headaches, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain after delivery are red flags for late-onset pre-eclampsia that need urgent medical attention.

question: What is the main reason for using a nursing theory in your research?

options.A: To dictate the exact medication dosage a patient must receive
options.B: To replace the need for ethical approval from the hospital board
options.C: To provide a structured framework for examining patient care
options.D: To calculate the monthly budget for the nursing unit

explanation: Theories act like a pair of glasses, helping us look at patient care in an organized and logical way.

question: How many actual sticky pads (electrodes) are placed on a patient for a standard 12-lead ECG?
explanation: Tricky question! We only put 10 physical pads on the body, and the machine does some math magic to show 12 different views.

question: What legal document outlines a patient's specific wishes regarding life-sustaining medical treatments?

options.A: A hospital discharge summary sheet
options.B: A physician prescription log
options.C: An advance directive or living will
options.D: A standard health insurance claim form

explanation: Living wills and advance directives legally document a person's preferences for medical interventions when they can no longer speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h7)

question: You check the drug label against the doctor's prescription order. Which 'right' are you making sure of?

options.A: Right Dose
options.B: Right Time
options.C: Right Route
options.D: Right Medication

explanation: Comparing the label directly to the prescription order is your foolproof way to confirm you've grabbed the exact right drug.

question: Why is a routine stool microscope check often not enough to tell exactly which Taenia species a patient has?

options.A: Eggs of different Taenia species look identical under the microscope.
options.B: Adult worms never release eggs into the digestive tract.
options.C: Tapeworm eggs dissolve completely in standard formalin preservatives.
options.D: Microscopes cannot magnify parasite structures clearly enough.

explanation: Exactly right! Under the microscope, the eggs of both species look almost the same, so just seeing an egg doesn't tell you if it's pork or beef tapeworm.

question: What is the safest way to prepare whole grapes before giving them to a young child?

options.A: Peeled and served whole
options.B: Soaked in warm water until soft
options.C: Cut into quarters lengthwise
options.D: Mashed into a smooth liquid paste

explanation: You got it! Cutting them lengthwise changes their round shape so they won't fit snugly and block a small airway.

question: Where must you place the specimen label before sending it to the lab?

options.A: On the nurse's clipboard holding paperwork
options.B: Only on the outside of the transport bag
options.C: On the examination table near the patient
options.D: Directly on the specimen container itself

explanation: Always label the actual container right away. This stops dangerous mix-ups if the sample gets separated from its outer bag in the lab.

question: Why are non-human reservoirs so important in the spread of diseases?

options.A: They purify local water sources so that waterborne parasites cannot infect people
options.B: They manufacture natural antibodies that help human populations fight off severe infections
options.C: They serve as temporary quarantine stations for individuals exposed to outbreaks
options.D: They provide a safe place for the infectious agent to survive and multiply over time

explanation: Spot on! Reservoirs act like safe breeding grounds for germs, making sure the disease cycle keeps going if we don't intervene.

question: In Herzberg's theory, what is the main job of 'hygiene factors' like basic pay and a clean workplace?

options.A: Guarantees that every worker will achieve self-actualization
options.B: Determining which clinical nurses receive a promotion
options.C: Preventing job dissatisfaction rather than creating deep motivation
options.D: Replacing the need for monetary compensation in public hospitals

explanation: Hygiene factors stop people from complaining (like fixing a broken fan or paying salaries on time), but true job love comes from other things like feeling valued.

question: As a nurse, what is your key responsibility when giving medications for hormone disorders?

options.A: Monitoring for expected therapeutic effects and potential adverse reactions
options.B: Prohibiting the patient from eating any food for 48 hours
options.C: Prescribing the initial starting dosage based on daily weight
options.D: Manufacturing synthetic hormone replacements in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Exactly! You are the patient's safety net—watching closely to see if the drug is helping and checking for any scary side effects.

question: As a nurse, what is your main goal when doing a risk assessment during antenatal care?

options.A: To accurately predict the exact day and hour of delivery
options.B: To eliminate the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: To detect potential complications early before they become life-threatening
options.D: To diagnose all genetic disorders in the unborn infant

explanation: Brilliant! Screening lets us spot moms who need extra support or specialized care early on, keeping both mother and baby safe.

question: Which factor directly causes a sudden drop in foetal oxygen due to mechanical compression?

options.A: Umbilical cord prolapse
options.B: Maternal mild anaemia
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Advanced maternal age

explanation: When the umbilical cord slips down before the baby, pressure from the presenting part compresses the cord and immediately blocks blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h2)

question: Why is it so important to treat strep throat quickly with antibiotics?

options.A: To ensure the patient never catches another cold ever again
options.B: To permanently shrink the size of the palatine tonsils
options.C: To cure viral rhinitis and clear nasal congestion instantly
options.D: To prevent serious systemic complications like rheumatic fever

explanation: Spot on! Early treatment stops strep bacteria from travelling around the body and causing serious issues like rheumatic heart disease.

question: A clinic expects to use 2,000 syringes during a vaccination drive. If each safety box holds 100 syringes, how many safety boxes are required?
explanation: Divide the total number of used syringes (2,000) by the capacity of a single box (100), which equals 20 boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why is transparency in reporting health funds crucial for community partnerships?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any volunteer labor in the school
options.B: It ensures that teachers receive higher bonuses each month
options.C: It prevents the government from inspecting school facilities
options.D: It builds mutual trust and encourages continued community support

explanation: When communities see how resources are used honestly, they remain willing to support and fund future school health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for Pick's disease?

options.A: Restoring lost brain tissue in the frontal lobe
options.B: Reversing the underlying cellular tau accumulation
options.C: Curing the primary neurodegenerative process
options.D: Managing behavioral symptoms and improving comfort

explanation: Since we can't cure or reverse the disease yet, our nursing care focuses on keeping the patient comfortable, calm, and managing tough behavioral symptoms.

question: Why does patient awareness nowadays push nursing practice to improve?

options.A: Patients expect safe, high-quality, and evidence-based care
options.B: Patients refuse to interact with newly graduated nurses
options.C: Patients prefer traditional remedies over hospital treatment
options.D: Patients demand complete control over hospital budgeting

explanation: Exactly! As people become more informed about their health rights, nurses step up their game to deliver safer, top-notch care.

question: What is the main purpose of a research design in nursing?

options.A: To calculate the final cost of the research project
options.B: To replace the need for an institutional review board
options.C: To format the bibliography of a research paper
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Think of a research design like an architectural blueprint. It gives you a clear, step-by-step plan to follow so you can find accurate answers to your clinical questions!

question: Why do pregnant women struggle so often with constipation?

options.A: Progesterone slows down normal bowel motility
options.B: Maternal kidneys absorb all water from the stool
options.C: The growing baby physically blocks the stomach
options.D: High protein diets stop intestinal movement

explanation: You got it! Pregnancy hormones relax smooth muscles all over the body, which unfortunately puts the brakes on digestion too.

question: What do we mean by 'closed-loop communication' during a busy medical emergency?

options.A: Repeating a delegated instruction back to the sender to confirm it was heard and understood
options.B: Writing all verbal orders on a whiteboard before speaking to team members
options.C: Turning off all ward intercoms so outside noise does not distract the team
options.D: Locking the patient room door so unauthorized staff cannot enter

explanation: Exactly! Saying 'Got it, giving 10mg IV now' back to the doctor or senior nurse prevents dangerous mistakes in high-stress moments.

question: How does eating too much salt contribute to high blood pressure?

options.A: It causes fluid retention which increases total blood volume.
options.B: It directly weakens the heart valves causing backflow.
options.C: It thickens the red blood cells so they cannot move easily.
options.D: It instantly melts the protective lining inside the veins.

explanation: Spot on! Salt (sodium) holds water in your body. This extra fluid increases the total volume of blood pushing against your vessel walls.

question: What happens to the solid particles in a drug suspension over time?

options.A: Solid particles are dispersed and tend to settle
options.B: Solid particles are fully dissolved in the liquid
options.C: Active ingredients are bound permanently to the bottle
options.D: The mixture remains completely clear at all times

explanation: Think of muddy water! Suspensions have tiny bits of medicine floating around that love to sink to the bottom if left alone. That's why we always shake them first!

question: If a patient has severe kidney failure, what adjustment would a nurse expect for a drug that is normally cleared by the kidneys?

options.A: Stopping all fluid intake to prevent the drug from diluting in the blood
options.B: Switching the patient immediately to a heavy lipid-soluble oral syrup
options.C: A reduction in the drug dose or an increased time interval between doses
options.D: Giving a double dose to overcome the buildup of metabolic waste

explanation: When kidneys aren't working at full speed, drugs stick around much longer. Nurses must watch out for this and expect lower doses or spaced-out timing to keep patients safe from toxicity!

question: A patient is admitted with severe vomiting and diarrhea. Which imbalance are they most at risk for developing?

options.A: Fluid and electrolyte imbalance
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: Permanent high blood pressure
options.D: Chronic respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Exactly! Vomiting and diarrhea flush out body fluids and essential minerals super fast, leaving the patient low on water and electrolytes.

question: A client with an inherited degenerative disorder shows early muscle weakness and clumsy coordination. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the client for emergency surgery to repair the damaged genes
options.B: Document the findings, report the progression to the healthcare team, and assess safety needs
options.C: Tell the family that these mild symptoms will completely disappear within a week
options.D: Advise the client to stop all physical movement immediately to prevent further weakness

explanation: Spotting these changes early and planning for safety helps protect the client from falls as their motor skills decline.

question: What solution is usually used to clean the skin before inserting the paracentesis needle?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide mixed with alcohol
options.B: Chlorhexidine or iodine antiseptic solution
options.C: Normal saline solution at room temperature
options.D: Warm sterile water and mild bath soap

explanation: Medical antiseptics like chlorhexidine or iodine are standard for killing skin germs before any procedure.

question: Which of these is an example of non-pharmacological (drug-free) pain relief?

options.A: Applying a warm compress to a sore muscle
options.B: Administering a prescribed dose of oral ibuprofen
options.C: Dispensing a scheduled narcotic pain pill
options.D: Injecting intravenous morphine into the patient port

explanation: You got it! Warm compresses, massage, and changing positions help ease pain without using drugs (pharmaceuticals).

question: Why is shouting directly at someone with hearing loss often a bad idea?

options.A: Shouting causes immediate physical pain inside the damaged middle ear bones
options.B: Raising your voice increases the pitch into a frequency range that is hard to understand
options.C: Loud sounds trigger defensive reflexes that close the outer ear canal completely
options.D: High volumes permanently destroy the remaining healthy hair cells in the cochlea

explanation: Makes sense, right? When we shout, our voice pitch goes up. Since age-related hearing loss usually steals high pitches first, shouting just makes your words sound more distorted, not clearer!

question: What is the very first step in a standard progressive discipline process?

options.A: Informal verbal warning
options.B: Immediate termination
options.C: Formal written warning
options.D: Temporary suspension

explanation: Progressive discipline starts gently with a private, verbal conversation to address minor issues early. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h5)

question: If a baby's head enters the pelvis leading with the longest chin-to-forehead (mentoventricular) measurement, what is the likely outcome?

options.A: Labour will proceed rapidly because this is the smallest skull measurement.
options.B: The baby is in an ideal position for a normal spontaneous delivery.
options.C: The head will easily mould to fit through the pelvic outlet without issues.
options.D: Vaginal birth is extremely difficult or impossible due to the large size.

explanation: At 14 centimeters, this is the biggest measurement of the head. It's too wide to easily fit through, which usually makes a normal vaginal delivery very difficult.

question: How should past studies be presented in a good literature review?

options.A: A random list of book titles found in the library
options.B: Unchecked rumors heard around the hospital ward
options.C: Personal diary entries written by the researcher
options.D: A critical analysis and grouping of past studies by themes

explanation: Instead of just listing past papers one by one, you group them by themes and discuss what they mean together.

question: Why does diabetes mellitus significantly increase a person's risk for developing CAD?

options.A: Pancreatic failure lowers the overall volume of body fluids
options.B: High blood sugar damages blood vessel linings over time
options.C: Extra sugar in the blood thickens the heart valves directly
options.D: Diabetes forces the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells

explanation: Chronic high blood glucose levels injure the delicate inner lining of arteries, making it much easier for plaque to form. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which dangerous emergency involves blood getting trapped inside the spleen, causing a sudden drop in blood volume?

options.A: Splenic sequestration crisis
options.B: Aplastic crisis
options.C: Megaloblastic crisis
options.D: Acute chest syndrome

explanation: In splenic sequestration, blood pools massively inside the spleen. This causes the spleen to swell rapidly and puts the patient into shock very quickly.

question: Transport fare and hospital registration costs can heavily influence whether a person visits the clinic. What kind of factor is this?

options.A: Pain tolerance level
options.B: Financial status
options.C: Biological immunity
options.D: Genetic predisposition

explanation: Money matters! Financial resources play a massive role in whether patients can afford to seek care or buy their drugs on time.

question: When dressing a stroke patient with weakness on one side, where should you put the clothes first?

options.A: Whichever side they prefer
options.B: The strong or unaffected side
options.C: Both sides at the exact same time
options.D: The weak or affected side

explanation: Brilliant! Dressing the weak side first saves the patient from painful, awkward twisting of a limb that lacks strength.

question: During non-surgical care for a kidney injury, which nursing sign is most important to report immediately?

options.A: An increase in sleepiness after receiving a scheduled pain medication
options.B: Mild bruising fading to a yellow color around the flank area
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure paired with a fast heart rate
options.D: A slight yellow tinge in the normal daily urine output

explanation: A fast heart rate and dropping blood pressure are early warning signs of hidden internal bleeding. Catching this early can save a life!

question: Why do nurses test for urinary ketones in a pregnant patient with severe vomiting?

options.A: It indicates the body is breaking down fat due to poor intake
options.B: It shows if the kidneys are failing from a bacterial infection
options.C: It rules out gestational diabetes mellitus completely
options.D: It confirms the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: Ketones mean the body has run out of easy energy and has started burning fat instead because the mum can't keep food down. It's a key sign to watch out for!

question: What is a major operational challenge when using MBO in a hospital?

options.A: Nurses refusing to care for patients under any circumstance
options.B: Patients demanding to set their own medical treatment goals
options.C: A complete lack of computers in all medical wards
options.D: Constant unpredictability and emergencies disrupting plans

explanation: Healthcare environments are volatile, making rigid adherence to long-term goals difficult during crises. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank.

question: What is the main goal of using medicine for glaucoma?

options.A: To lower pressure inside the eye and protect the optic nerve
options.B: To increase blood flow directly to the retina and lens
options.C: To cure bacterial infections in the cornea
options.D: To widen the pupil and improve night vision

explanation: You've got this! In glaucoma, fluid builds up and creates pressure. Our main goal is to relieve that pressure so the delicate optic nerve stays safe from damage.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask a fainting patient about visual changes before the event?

options.A: It indicates that permanent blindness is about to occur.
options.B: It helps confirm a vasovagal prodrome rather than sudden cardiac arrest.
options.C: It proves the patient has an underlying eye disease.
options.D: It shows that the patient's blood sugar was extremely high.

explanation: Cardiac syncope usually strikes instantly without warning, whereas vasovagal syncope gives prodromal visual and physical signs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: A surgeon has to remove the very last section of a patient's small intestine. Which part is this?

options.A: Duodenum
options.B: Ileum
options.C: Jejunum
options.D: Sigmoid colon

explanation: The ileum is the final stretch of the small intestine right before it hands over food waste to the large intestine. Great job remembering that!

question: Why are the standard 'rights' of medication administration so important if a legal case of negligence arises?

options.A: They are federal tax requirements for pharmaceutical companies.
options.B: They serve as the accepted standard of care to prove or disprove negligence.
options.C: They guarantee that hospitals will never face patient lawsuits.
options.D: They allow doctors to bypass writing paper prescriptions.

explanation: Exactly! The medication rights represent everyday nursing best practices. Courts look at them to see if standard care was followed.

question: When might a doctor perform a procedure like a D&C (dilatation and curettage) for a patient with endometritis?

options.A: When retained products of conception are present in the uterus
options.B: When the white blood cell count returns to normal
options.C: When the patient develops a mild skin rash
options.D: When the patient refuses to take oral medications

explanation: If tiny bits of the placenta are left behind, they act like food for bacteria. A D&C helps clean out that leftover tissue so the infection can finally heal.

question: What is your very first action if a patient's neurological condition suddenly and unexpectedly worsens?

options.A: Ask a family member to monitor the patient for an hour
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to help the patient rest
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately and report the changes
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to write it in the main chart

explanation: Sudden neuro changes are an emergency. Quick reporting saves lives, so always alert the doctor or senior nurse right away.

question: Which combination of vital signs points directly to Cushing's triad?

options.A: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.B: High fever, hypertension, and excessive sweating
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, and normal breathing patterns
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, and rapid deep breathing

explanation: Cushing's triad is a late, serious sign of high brain pressure. It's the body's desperate, failing attempt to pump blood into a squeezed brain. Great clinical spot!

question: What is the main goal of doing a community risk assessment?

question: What exactly is a 'tropic' hormone?

question: How do viruses usually spread through food compared to bacteria?

question: Why must a nurse check that a patient hasn't eaten or drunk anything (NPO status) before a scheduled laryngoscopy?

question: An instructor gives you tips on your sterile technique halfway through your ward posting so you can fix your mistakes. What kind of evaluation is this?

question: What is one of the most important daily fluid instructions to give a patient managing gout?

question: A choking patient suddenly passes out and falls to the floor. What should you do right away?

question: What is the main goal of using a steam tent for a patient?

question: Why is inventory control considered a vital duty for ward nurses?

question: Why do cancer cells keep growing even after the original tissue injury is gone?

question: Why should a nurse ask non-judgmental questions when assessing a patient's medication habits?

question: Why do pregnant women often feel the need to urinate frequently?

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

question: What is the primary advantage of intravenous therapy over oral medication administration?

question: Why does a malnourished patient usually take longer to recover from an infection?
